findings.trigger: An explicitly acknowledged POST reaches a controlled request-acceptance stub, then transport or response decoding fails, or a gateway returns failure.
findings.observed: Sell claims the order was not created; malformed buy response recommends trying again; other responses expose technical error text without checking whether an order exists.
findings.impact: A response failure cannot establish noncreation; wording can encourage duplicate order attempts. No actual persisted order, customer incident or payment duplication is claimed.
findings.requiredBoundary: Represent unknown outcome neutrally, direct the user to existing order status before another attempt, preserve explicit validation errors and one-request-per-acknowledgement.

findings.trigger: Start two preparations; resolve newer, cancel its review, then resolve older.
findings.observed: The older response opens a new visible review after explicit cancellation. No signature occurs solely from this response.
findings.impact: Cancellation does not invalidate pending preparation and the UI resurrects an abandoned operation.
findings.requiredBoundary: Invalidate or serialize preparation across cancellation/supersession; a stale response must not revive abandoned confirmation.

findings.trigger: Confirm one prepared transaction while fake sendTransaction remains unresolved, then open and confirm a second review.
findings.observed: The application invokes sendTransaction twice before the first promise settles. Each invocation still required a fresh acknowledgement.
findings.impact: The application does not serialize unresolved wallet handoffs. Actual wallet SDK/Telegram behavior and double execution are unverified.
findings.requiredBoundary: Guard unresolved handoffs; preserve explicit cancellation/failure and avoid duplicate UI-triggered calls before wallet outcome is known.

preservedControls: Opening review does not create a buy/sell order.
Unacknowledged or explicitly cancelled wallet review cannot sign.
Two confirm events on one acknowledged review invoke one wallet handoff.
Rejected synthetic wallet signature never calls send-signed.
Existing primitive buy/sell form snapshots and literal memo tests remain applicable.
limits: All probes are deterministic exact-source function scenarios with inert external boundaries.
No live wallet, provider, customer request, database, network, message or runtime mutation.
Synthetic request acceptance demonstrates insufficient response evidence; it does not prove real backend persistence.
Findings concern these bounded transitions, not full E4 gate closure.
